rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP. LXI. A Fugitive Servant, which way gone, when returne?
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: Chapter LXI introduces a worked question about a servant who had fled, asking where he went and when he would return.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Chapter begins beneath the LX marriage divider; do not conflate with LX marriage case or LXII missing-dog case.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: A Servant Fled
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: The original 1647 image contains a distinct square horoscope headed A Servant Fled with house and planetary symbols.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Original diagram, not an independently calculated ephemeris; no exact date, birthplace or timezone is stated in this figure.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Judgment upon the Figure foregoing.
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: The author explicitly connects the judgment on printed page 391 to the preceding original fugitive-servant figure.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Opening of the worked judgment, not a general independently tested predictive rule.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: ascendant and Mercury in Aquarius, together with Mars posited in ascendant
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: The ascendant, Mercury in Aquarius and Mars placed in the ascendant are used to characterize the servant’s master.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Distinct from Mars serving as fugitive significator in this figure; source applies both roles according to context.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Master ... short of stature, corpulent ... ruddy, fresh countenance
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: The master is characterized as short, heavyset, healthy-complexioned and ruddy-faced.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Reported case description without external identification or anthropometric records.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: fatnesse ... north latitude of Mercury ... about one degree
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: The author attributes the master’s fatness partly to Mercury having approximately one degree of northern latitude.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Qualitative author explanation, not empirically calibrated physiognomy.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: degrees ascending ... Terms of Mars ... ayery Signe ... Face or Decanate of Sun
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: He further invokes the rising degree in Mars terms, an airy sign, and the Sun’s face or decan.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Specific original dignity language, no normalized terms table or contemporary sign-trait diagnosis.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun ... in a watry Signe ... partill trine to Moon
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: The Sun in a watery sign and an exact trine to the Moon are included among the author’s body-type premises.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: The original states both planets are in moist signs; original scan glyphs are controlling.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: argued a flegmatick, full body
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: The author draws a phlegmatic/full-body conclusion from the listed moist and other chart conditions.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Historical humoral theory, not a validated health or temperament assessment.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Significator of Servant was Mars peculiarly in this Figure
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: Mars is specifically assigned as significator of the missing servant in this case.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: The author explicitly distinguishes chart-specific Mars from his usual Mercury assignment.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: although many times Mercury shall signifie a fugitive Servant
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: He notes Mercury often signifies a fugitive servant in other judgments.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Do not override the present case’s expressly selected Mars significator.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: young Fellow of about nineteen
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: The missing servant is described as a young man approximately 19 years old.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Historical narrative about an unidentified person; not corroborated by surviving records.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: well set ... short, big joynted, broad and full faced, dark browne haire
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: The author describes a short, strongly jointed, broad-faced young man with dark brown hair.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Author-reported appearance cannot validate astrology traits without independent data.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: his teeth growing ilsavouredly ... Sun-burnt ... skin ... cleer
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: Additional details concern irregular teeth, sunburnt/dark outward complexion and clear skin elsewhere.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: The source differentiates face from body; avoid flattening or treating as pathology.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: went away from his Master the Sunday preceding
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: The servant is reported to have left on the Sunday preceding the consultation.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: The printed figure does not provide a question date, so elapsed days to Friday cannot be independently computed.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: at which time the Moon was in Gemini, a Westerne Signe
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: The author relates the Moon’s alleged Gemini position at departure to a westerly direction.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Historical chart symbolism; cannot independently validate departure time or sign.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: now Mars, Significator ... in same Signe
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: At the consultation Mars is said to occupy Gemini, the same sign as the Moon at the servant’s departure.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Relative dates and referents retained; no exact calculation from missing event times.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Mercury ... in Aquarius, a Westerne Signe ... South quarter
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: Mercury in Aquarius is described as a westerly sign located in the southern quarter of the sky.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: The author also discusses Gemini’s southern and Aquarius’s northern quarter associations.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Gemini hath ... South ... Aquarius ... North
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: The author notes different cardinal-quarter associations in addition to sign-based directional meaning.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Do not mechanically substitute one cardinal rule for another.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Servant went westward at his first departing
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: Lilly reports having judged that the missing servant initially traveled westward.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: This is the author’s self-reported forecast, not an authenticated original dated prediction.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: at the time of the Question ... West from the querents house
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: He reports judging the servant was west of the master’s home when asked.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: No independent location record at consultation time.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Mars was angular ... every way as strong as Moon
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: Mars is preferred because the author judges him angular and as strong as the Moon.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: He says otherwise he would have judged by the Moon; retain this priority condition.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Mars Significator ... Mercury Lord of ascendant ... hastening to a trine
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: Mars and Mercury are described as approaching a trine while leaving angular houses.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Direction and role assignments are central; not a retrospective numerical ephemeris model.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: within a day or two ... have his Servant againe
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: The author claims to have forecast the servant returning within one or two days of the consultation.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Exact consultation date unprovided here; cannot compare the interval against the reported Friday return.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon in second, in her owne house ... Servant part of Masters Estate
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: The author uses a Moon in the second house, its own house, together with estate symbolism.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Do not infer literal ownership of people or convert this into present-day norms.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Master should not lose ... recover forthwith his lost Goods
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: Lilly says he forecast that the master would recover missing goods and avoid a loss.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: The later narrative reports return but does not independently confirm specific goods or value.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon ... perfect trine of Sun in eleventh ... both Moiety ascending
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: He adduces an exact Moon–Sun trine between the second and eleventh houses, with source-specific moiety wording.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Original diagram and text are the authority; no modern orb or scoring weight inferred.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: neerenesse of Mars to degree ascending
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: The closing paragraph cites Mars being near the ascendant degree as relevant to distance.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: The sentence crosses from bottom of original PDF425 to top of PDF426.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: not above three or four houses Westward
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: The author says he expected the servant to be only three or four houses west of the master’s dwelling.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: A distinctive concrete distance claim, not obviously the same as the subsequent claim of Kingston upon Thames.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Friday following betimes in the morning, he came home
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: The author states that the servant returned home early on the following Friday.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Source-internal report; no court, servant, household or external dated record corroborates the return.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: said he had been at Kingston upon Thames
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: The returned servant reportedly said he had stayed at Kingston upon Thames.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: This is hearsay narrated by Lilly, not observed location at the consultation.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: which if true
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: The author explicitly qualifies the servant’s statement about Kingston with the words “which if true.”
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Preserve uncertainty rather than treat the Kingston account as independently confirmed.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: full West, or a little to South, and neer a great Water ... Thames
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: Lilly interprets the claimed Kingston visit as westerly or slightly southerly and near the Thames.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: Retrospective geographic alignment; note tension with the earlier three-or-four-houses distance estimate.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: as Moon in Cancer did or might signifie
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: He offers the Moon in Cancer as a possible signification of the nearby water.
rows.conditions_source_limits_or_chronology: The original uses tentative “did or might”; no independent positional confirmation.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP. LXII. A Dogge missing, where?
rows.historical_author_report_paraphrase: Chapter LXII on a missing dog begins below the divider, with its own figure; all of its body is excluded.
